thread:
maya: Quick preflight update — our synthetic load on eu-west3-gpu-pool shows persistent egress tail spikes around 02:30->03:15 UTC. Not huge errors but sustained queueing that pushed some tail latencies above SLA by ~120ms.
sergio: ack. did we correlate to a specific rack or nic driver?
maya: initial look points at racks r04-r06 (nics with older fw). Packet drops + flow-control backpressure during big KV cache flush.
sergio: ugh. that matches the health dump from last night. can you paste the skyline graphs?
maya: attaching quick snippets from the agent: (sketch) egress qlen spikes on r04/r05, slightly elevated retransmits on r06. not a whole-cluster outage but enough to risk noisy neighbors during planned maintenance.
infra-bot: deploy-checker: cluster eu-west3: 3/120 nodes showing >5% retry rate in last 1h.
maya: proposal: 1) schedule a short maintenance window 03:00-04:30 UTC next Tue, rolling 2-rack hot-swap + NIC fw micro-upgrade; 2) route high-priority Serving traffic to eu-west1 fallback for that window; 3) use reserved burst capacity (dedicated) to avoid consumer-facing rate limits.
tasha: timeline + fallback sounds good. how many GPUs will we move and what's the expected cost delta for the burst?
maya: estimate ~160 GPUs (~10% of cluster). If we push those to Dedicated burst it'll add an incremental cost ~30-40% for the 90min window versus normal spot mix. ballpark $4-6k for the window.
sergio: can we instead reroute only critical routes (prod-tokenized) and keep eval/low-prio on eu-west3 to reduce cost?
maya: yes — routing by priority is straightforward. Redwood router can pin customer-tier routes. We'll add a routing rule: if route.priority >= 90 -> eu-west1, else keep.
oncall: what about throughput impact on eu-west1? do we have capacity headroom?
devops: eu-west1 has ~200 idle GPUs in the spare pool; should absorb burst at <20% util. We'll set autoscale buffer + pre-warm 40 GPUs 15m before window to avoid cold-start lag.
sergio: runbook snippets? want to ensure drainage + KV cache warm-up steps are explicit.
maya: runbook draft: ```
1. 02:30 UTC: pre-warm 40 GPUs in eu-west1 (preprovision API)
2. 02:45 UTC: update routing rules (priority-based) and verify 95th p99 latency on a smoke set
3. 03:00 UTC: begin rack hot-swap r04 -> cordon & drain nodes (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data)
4. 03:15 UTC: apply NIC fw micro-upgrade on r04, reboot nodes one at a time
5. 03:45 UTC: rejoin nodes, verify telemetry and packet counters
6. 04:00 UTC: repeat for r05
7. 04:20 UTC: validate end-to-end latency and cost telemetry, revert routing rules at 04:30 if green
```
sergio: add step to warm KV caches on eu-west1 for pinned models: run small prefix-replay to populate KV before moving real traffic.
maya: noted — will add prefix-replay script to step 2.
tasha: communication plan: send customer-facing notice to enterprise customers in eu-west3 (72h), post #status 24h before, and include fallback details + expected minor latency increase for noncritical routes.
devops: I'll open the RFC and tag infra-oncall + eng-sre. also will create an ops-run channel for the window.
infra-bot: rfc-bot: RFC-4321 created: preflight-egress-hot-swap. Link: https://rfc.internal/RFC-4321
oncall: if anything looks off during r04 work, pause and escalate to oncall immediately — do not complete r05 without signoff.
maya: agreed. signing off on runbook + cost calc. will attach perf smoke script and timeline in RFC.
tasha: approved from PM side, ping sales for heads-up to affected customers.
sergio: thanks — I'll prep the drain scripts and NIC fw playbook. let's keep the window narrow and prefer rollback to incremental repeats if instability crops up. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks all. will merge RFC and schedule maintenance window with calendar invite and #ops-run channel.
infra-bot: reminder set: maintenance-start in 48h (ops-run channel).
